Let \(S_y = 7^y + 12y - 1\). We seek the gcd of all \(S_y\).

- \(S_1 = 18\)
- \(S_2 = 72\)

So the gcd divides \(\gcd(18,72)=18\).

Now show every \(S_y\) is divisible by \(18\). Mod \(2\):

\[
7^y + 12y - 1 \equiv 1 + 0 - 1 \equiv 0 \pmod 2.
\]

Mod \(9\), since \(7 \equiv -2 \pmod 9\), inductively:

\[
S_{y+1} - S_y = 7^{y+1} + 12(y+1) - 1 - (7^y + 12y - 1)
= 6(7^y + 2).
\]

Since \(7^y + 2 \equiv 1 + 2 \equiv 0 \pmod 3\), we get \(6(7^y+2)\) divisible by \(18\). With \(S_1=18\), all \(S_y\) are divisible by \(18\).

Thus the largest such \(x\) is \(\gcd\{S_y\}=18\).

\[
\boxed{18}
\]
